en: The Sūtra on Subduing Lust, translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmakṣema of the Western Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika approached the Blessed One; having arrived, he prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.
Once the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was standing to one side, he addressed the Blessed One, saying:
"Indeed, World-Honored One!
How many types of those who have subdued lust can be known in the world?
"O householder!"
In the world, there are ten ways of suppressing lust.

What are these ten? This householder may suppress lust in one way: he engages in unlawful sexual conduct with another; he seeks unlawful sexual gratification without employing skillful means; having thus brought suffering upon himself, he finds no peace for his own person, nor does he bring peace to his parents, wife, children, guests, servants, or slaves; nor does he bring benefit to śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas; nor does he perform deeds that lead to goodness or rebirth in the heavens.
Thus it is, householder!
This is one who has subdued lust.

Furthermore, householder, there may be another who has subdued lust, who seeks sexual intercourse unrighteously with others and seeks sexual intercourse unrighteously for himself, yet provides security for himself, his parents, wife and children, guests, messengers, and servants, and does not give to śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas; because of this goodness, he attains a good rebirth and is born in a good destination.
"In this way, householder,
this is one who has subdued lust.
Furthermore, householder:

Or, one may occasionally subdue lust and refrain from seeking illicit union with others; having refrained from such illicit pursuit, they bring peace and security to themselves, their parents, their wife and children, and their guests, servants, and slaves; they are able to give to śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas, and by performing this good deed, they attain a wholesome body and are reborn in a favorable realm.
"In this way, householder,
this is one who has subdued lust.
Furthermore, householder:

Or, one may subdue lust and seek wealth in accordance with the Dharma; having sought wealth in accordance with the Dharma, they do not use it for their own bodily pleasure, nor for the sake of their parents, nor for their wife and children, nor for their slaves and servants, nor do they give it as alms to śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas; yet, by virtue of this goodness, they attain a good rebirth and are born in a favorable realm.
"In this way, householder, one is a subduer of lust.
Furthermore, householder, there is another who is a subduer of lust:

he seeks wealth in accordance with the Dharma; having sought wealth in accordance with the Dharma, he brings happiness to himself, his parents, his wife and children, and his servants and slaves, yet he does not give anything to śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas. Because of this goodness, he attains a good rebirth and is born in a good destination."
In this way, householder,
this is one who has subdued lust.
Furthermore, householder:

Or, one may subdue lust and seek wealth in accordance with the Dharma; having sought wealth in accordance with the Dharma, they bring peace and happiness to themselves, their parents, wives, children, and servants, and bestow it upon śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas; by performing such good deeds, they attain a good rebirth and are born in a favorable realm.
In this way, householder,
this is one who has subdued lust.
Furthermore, householder:

Or, one may subdue lust by seeking wealth according to the Dharma, neither encroaching upon others nor encroaching upon oneself; yet, one does not seek personal comfort for the body, nor for the sake of parents, wife, children, or servants, nor does one give it away to śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas—doing good so as to obtain a good body and be born in a good realm.
"In this way, householder,
this is one who has subdued lust.
Furthermore, householder:

Or, one may subdue lust and seek wealth according to the Dharma, neither encroaching upon others nor encroaching upon oneself; thus, one attains peace and happiness for oneself, one’s parents, wife, children, and servants, yet does not bestow anything upon śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas. By performing such good deeds, one obtains a good body and is reborn in a good realm.
In this way, householder,
this is one who has subdued lust.
Furthermore, householder:

Or, one may subdue lust, seeking wealth according to the Dharma without encroaching upon others and seeking wealth according to the Dharma without encroaching upon oneself; thus attaining peace and happiness for oneself, as well as for one’s parents, wife, children, and servants, and giving to śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas, one performs good deeds, attains a good body, and is born in a good realm.
Having obtained that wealth, he becomes attached to it and deeply infatuated with it; he does not perceive its perilous consequences, nor does he know how to renounce it, yet he greedily consumes it.
Thus it is, householder!
This is one way of subduing lust.
"Furthermore, householder, there is another who subdues lust:

he seeks wealth righteously without encroaching upon others, and he seeks wealth righteously without encroaching upon himself; thus he attains peace and security for himself, as well as for his parents, wife, children, and servants. He bestows gifts upon śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas, performing good deeds so that he may attain a good body and be reborn in a good realm."

When he obtains wealth, he is neither defiled by it nor attached to it; he does not take pleasure in it, nor does he dwell within it. He recognizes it as a calamity and a transformation, and is thus able to relinquish it while still consuming it.
"In this way, householder,
this is one who has subdued lust.
This, householder!"

Suppose one person suppresses their lust and seeks wealth through unrighteous means; having sought wealth through unrighteous means, they find no peace for themselves, nor do they bring peace to their parents, wife, children, or servants. Furthermore, they do not give gifts to śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas, nor do they perform good deeds to attain a good rebirth in a favorable realm.
This, householder, is how one subdues lust.
I declare that such a person has subdued lust; I call this the overcoming of evil.
"Householder! Suppose one suppresses lust for a single day;

though he wrongfully seeks wealth from others and wrongfully seeks wealth for himself, he keeps his own person, as well as his parents, wife, children, and servants, in safety and comfort. He does not give to śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas, yet by doing good, he attains a good rebirth and is born in a good destination."
"Householder!
This is the subduing of lust; this is the subduing of lust. It is a small victory, a small victory.
"Householder! [he continued].

He may be one who subdues lust, seeking wealth according to the Dharma without encroaching upon others, and seeking wealth according to the Dharma without encroaching upon himself; thus he attains peace and happiness for his own person, as well as for his parents, wife, children, and servants. He gives to śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas, and by performing such good deeds, he attains a good body and is reborn in a good realm.
When he obtains wealth, he is neither stained nor attached to it, neither grasps at it nor delights in it; knowing it to be a calamity and a transformation, he abandons it and consumes it.
It is thus.
"Householder!
Sexual indulgence is the most excellent, the most wonderful, the highest, the best, and the unsurpassed victory.
It is just as if, householder!"

There is cow’s milk; from milk comes curd, from curd comes cream-of-curds (maṇḍa), from cream-of-curds comes butter, and from butter comes clarified butter (ghṛta). This is the most excellent, most wonderful, and unsurpassed teaching.
In this way, householder!
These various subduings of lust—such as these subduings of lust—are the most excellent and sublime, the most exquisite and supreme, the unsurpassed and peerless.
A verse was spoken:
"Wealth accumulated through unrighteous means, though given according to the Dharma, is not truly given;
if one neither consumes it nor gives it away for the sake of merit, it is as if it were never given at all."
Both are defiled by stinginess; this lust is the food of evil conduct.
If one seeks wealth according to the Dharma with the desire to give for the sake of merit, then both giving it away and consuming it can produce meritorious virtue.
Neither of the two is defiled by stinginess; both possess this subduing of lust.
One who is able to practice wisdom subdues lust according to their conduct;
knowing transformation and possessing contentment, they eat with contentment.
"One who is able to practice wisdom is most wondrously capable of subduing lust.
Thus spoke the Buddha; having heard what the World-Honored One had said, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika rejoiced and was gladdened.
The Sūtra on Subduing Lust Spoken by the Buddha
